meaning: A gentle, indirect way of persuading that builds good feelings about a brand instead of pushing people to buy.
example: The bank's advert is a soft sell: a quiet story about a father teaching his daughter to ride a bike, with the logo only at the end.
group: Persuasion 说服手法

meaning: Influence someone in a clever or unfair way, so that they do what you want without fully realising it.
example: Critics say the jingling coin sounds in the mobile game are designed to manipulate children into spending.
group: Persuasion 说服手法

meaning: A short phrase that goes with a brand name or logo and is used across all its adverts for a long time.
example: The supermarket's strapline, 'Good food for every table', appears under its logo on bags, vans and adverts.
group: Language of adverts 广告语言

meaning: The main block of text in a printed advert, under the headline, giving the details.
example: The body copy of the hiking boot advert describes the waterproof leather in three short paragraphs.
group: Language of adverts 广告语言

meaning: Extreme exaggeration that is not meant to be taken literally.
example: The pillow advert's hyperbole promises 'sleep like you're floating on a cloud of kittens'.
group: Language of adverts 广告语言

meaning: A newly invented word, or an old word used in a new way.
example: The chocolate brand builds its new advert around a neologism: 'chocolicious'.
group: Language of adverts 广告语言

meaning: The way an advert speaks to its audience, for example chatty, serious, bossy or flattering.
example: The mode of address in the teen skincare advert is chatty and jokey, as if a big sister were talking.
group: Language of adverts 广告语言
note: Also in Representation: separate entry, advertising meaning and example.

meaning: The job words do in an advert when they tell us how to read an image, closing down its other possible meanings.
example: A photo of an empty road could mean anything, but the line 'Freedom starts here' provides anchorage for the car advert.
zh: 锚定（文字固定图像意义）
group: Language of adverts 广告语言
note: Also in Representation: separate entry, advertising meaning and example.

meaning: Official rules about what adverts may say and show, and the work of making sure the rules are followed.
example: Because of regulation, the junk food adverts cannot be shown during children's programmes.
group: The advertising business 广告行业

meaning: A short statement that limits what a company promises or is responsible for.
example: The diet pill advert ends with a fast disclaimer: 'Results may vary.'
group: The advertising business 广告行业

meaning: Changing a photo, now usually on a computer, to remove marks and make people look slimmer or smoother.
example: After complaints about airbrushing, the make-up brand promised to stop smoothing its models' skin.
group: Representation in adverts 广告中的再现

meaning: A theory that a successful advert leads the audience through four steps: attention, interest, desire and action.
example: Following the AIDA model, the trainer advert grabs attention with a crash of drums, builds interest and desire with the shoes in action, and ends with 'Buy now'.
zh: AIDA模式（注意—兴趣—欲望—行动）
group: Theory and debates 理论与争论

meaning: Abraham Maslow's idea that the things humans must have form a pyramid, from food and safety at the bottom to love, respect and fulfilment at the top.
example: The home insurance advert speaks to the safety level of the hierarchy of needs, while the perfume advert aims higher, at love and status.
group: Theory and debates 理论与争论

meaning: The theory that audiences actively choose media to meet their own needs, such as information, entertainment or a sense of identity.
example: Uses and gratifications theory helps explain why people happily share funny adverts online: they are looking for entertainment.
group: Theory and debates 理论与争论

meaning: The study of signs and how they create meaning, used to analyse the images, colours and words in adverts.
example: Using semiotics, we can read the white coat in the toothpaste advert as a sign of science and trust.
group: Theory and debates 理论与争论

meaning: The physical form of a sign: the image, word, colour or sound that we actually see or hear.
example: In the perfume advert, the red rose is the signifier, and love is what it stands for.
group: Theory and debates 理论与争论

meaning: The idea or meaning that a sign stands for in the audience's mind.
example: The signified of the gold crown on the beer label is royalty and quality.
group: Theory and debates 理论与争论

meaning: The way a powerful group's ideas come to seem normal and natural, so that most people accept them without question.
example: Decades of car adverts showing happy families in the suburbs helped build a hegemony in which owning a car seemed essential to a good life.
group: Theory and debates 理论与争论

meaning: Changing or copying real adverts to make fun of them and criticise the companies or the message behind them.
example: In an act of subvertising, someone changed an oil company's billboard so that its sunny beach was covered in black oil.
group: Theory and debates 理论与争论

meaning: Disrupting adverts and mass media, often with humour or art, to make people question a life built around buying things.
example: The culture jamming group stuck fake price tags reading 'Do you need this?' on goods in a shopping centre.
group: Theory and debates 理论与争论

meaning: A way of life, or a society, in which buying and owning things is seen as the main road to happiness.
example: The phone advert's message that a new model every year will make you happy is a clear example of consumerism.
group: Consumer culture 消费文化

meaning: Caring more about money and possessions than about people, ideas or experiences.
example: The music video celebrates materialism: piles of cash, designer bags and a garage full of sports cars.
group: Consumer culture 消费文化

meaning: Something that is bought and sold, especially when it is treated as nothing more than a product.
example: For the free video app, viewers' attention is the real commodity that it sells to advertisers.
group: Consumer culture 消费文化

meaning: Turning something that is not usually sold, such as a feeling, a tradition or a relationship, into a product to make money.
example: Critics see the commodification of friendship in the advert, which suggests you can buy closeness with matching bracelets.
group: Consumer culture 消费文化

meaning: Buying expensive things mainly to show other people how rich or important you are.
example: The luxury car advert celebrates conspicuous consumption: the driver pulls up slowly so that everyone outside the restaurant turns to look.
group: Consumer culture 消费文化

meaning: Designing products to break or go out of date quickly, so that customers have to buy new ones.
example: The phone company's promise of an 'all-new design' every year fits a pattern of planned obsolescence.
group: Consumer culture 消费文化

meaning: When one media text refers to, borrows from or copies another well-known text, expecting the audience to recognise it.
example: The intertextuality in the crisps advert is obvious: it copies a famous shower scene from a horror film, but the scream is about an empty packet.
group: Language of adverts 广告语言

meaning: An imitation of a well-known text that exaggerates its style to make fun of it.
example: The sparkling water advert is a parody of perfume adverts: the same slow motion and whispering, but over a glass of fizzy water.
group: Language of adverts 广告语言

meaning: A text that imitates the style of another text or period with affection, as a tribute rather than to mock it.
example: The bakery's advert is a pastiche of 1950s cartoons, with bouncing loaves and a cheerful old-fashioned narrator.
group: Language of adverts 广告语言

meaning: Making a company or product look much kinder to the environment than it really is.
example: Critics accused the oil company of greenwashing when its advert showed nothing but wind turbines and forests.
group: The advertising business 广告行业

meaning: Promotion that shows women and girls as strong, capable and confident, often to sell products to them.
example: The sports bra campaign is femvertising: women of every size sprint, lift and shout, with no mention of looking slim.
group: The advertising business 广告行业

meaning: Exaggerated praise in adverts, like 'the best coffee in the world', which nobody could prove or disprove.
example: 'The tastiest pizza in the universe' is puffery: no one can test it, so it is allowed.
group: The advertising business 广告行业

meaning: Tricks in the design of websites and apps that push people into choices they did not mean to make, such as signing up or paying more.
example: The subscription page uses dark patterns: the 'Cancel' button is grey and tiny, while 'Keep my plan' is big and bright.
group: The advertising business 广告行业
